upsertSlices.label: Random-graph edge coloring: how rare is failure?
upsertSlices.task: A polynomial algorithm and the probability that the requested palette is impossible.
assumptions: The axis measures an exponential failure-probability coefficient, not time or palette size. Hollow anchors show ε→0 references; exact inequalities retain ε. Green certifies low algorithm failure; red limits how rare failure can be because some inputs are infeasible.

axis.label: See scoped figure panels; incompatible objectives have separate axes

results.guarantee: Find a proper Δ-edge-coloring when the algorithm succeeds
results.notes: General fixed 0<p<1 bound is O(exp(−c n log n/2)) for c<min(p/2,1/3). Marker1/8 is a limiting exponent, not the value for fixedε.

results.guarantee: Any attempted Δ-coloring must fail on class-2 inputs
results.notes: This is unavoidable infeasibility, not a running-time lower bound. The primary formula is exp(−n(log n+O(log log n))/2).
